messages:
maya (support): FYI: ACME reporting sudden 502 spikes on hosted inference during long streaming responses (~>4k tokens). Started ~08:10 PST, affects a few tenants only.
acme-ops (customer): Seeing 502s on streamed completions, started after a heavy batch job. curl shows connection reset mid-stream. trace-id: trace-ACME-3110
leo (eng-runtime): Can you paste a repro curl/headers? curious if it's h2 keepalive / windowing related or upstream conn reuse.
acme-ops (customer): Repro command: ```curl -v -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=grove-large -d '{"prompt":"long..."}'``` we get HTTP/2 502 and then RST_STREAM from upstream.
jonathan (sre): Envoy stats show short bursts of 502 downstream with upstream reset reason=connection_failure around same times. Also h2.active_streams spiking on ingress.
leo (eng-runtime): That fits h2 multiplex pool exhaustion. For streaming models we keep long-lived streams so connection slots get occupied. If upstreams drop for auth or billing checks we can see RSTs.
maya (support): Customer says this only started after recent model rollout (bigger tokens). Could be more concurrent stream time.
ingress-proxy-bot: Deploy event: routed v2-runtime patch to region-us-west at 07:58 PST (deploy id dpl-20260310-42). No rollout flags.
leo (eng-runtime): Two quick checks: 1) confirm auth backend latency spikes (jwt validation/cache TTL). 2) inspect upstream keepalive timeouts. jonathan can you pull envoy upstream_retries and h2 pool metrics per host?
jonathan (sre): Pulling now. Early look: auth backend p95 jumped to 420ms during the window; upstream idle-timeout for some hosts is 30s. Also see conn_pool_exhausted counters increment.
acme-ops (customer): We can throttle requests on our side but need a root cause. Any temporary mitigation we can flip on your side?
leo (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: increase h2 keepalive max streams per connection on ingress and bump connection pool cap for region-us-west. Also consider reducing auth cache TTL to avoid auth calls per-request during peak.
maya (support): I'll open an infra ticket for pool bump and ask infra to coordinate a safe change. Also passing suggested workaround to ACME: reduce concurrency and enable retry-on-502 with exponential backoff.
jonathan (sre): Rolling a small pool increase now to test (non-disruptive): bumping h2.max_streams from 100 to 200 on a subset of nodes.
leo (eng-runtime): Watch for head-of-line issues; if this reduces RSTs that's likely pool saturation. If still happening we need tcp resets trace and kernel-level retransmit logs.
deploy-bot: Partial config change applied to ingress-nodeset-3: h2.max_streams=200 (change id cfg-3312). Monitor window 5m.
maya (support): ACME confirmed 15m after change 502s dropped to baseline. They still saw occasional long-tail 504s for very long responses but much improved.
leo (eng-runtime): Next actions: 1) schedule proper autoscaling of connection pools; 2) add alerting on conn_pool_exhausted and auth p95; 3) evaluate prefix/KV caching for long-lived streams to reduce auth calls.
acme-ops (customer): Thanks — will keep an eye and report regressions. Appreciate quick response :thumbsup:
maya (support): I'll file postmortem + customer summary. Tagging @oncall for follow-up and documentation update for streaming model guidance.
jonathan (sre): Will attach envoy traces & graphs to the ticket (internal link) and propose safe defaults for h2 params.
leo (eng-runtime): Also add a small note to runbook: "If streaming 502 spike — check auth latency, conn_pool_exhausted, deploy window, then consider pool bump + retry throttling."
